name: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung (FES) Scholarship for International Students

universities: Any state or state-recognised German university / university of applied sciences

duration: Up to the maximum funding period under BAföG regulations (i.e. roughly the standard period of study); a degree programme of fewer than 3 semesters is not funded
eligibleNationalities: Students from the Global South (Asia, Africa, Latin America), post-Soviet states, and eastern/south-eastern European (EU) countries. Students/doctoral candidates from OECD countries are NOT eligible. Bangladesh (non-OECD, Asia) is eligible — but the applicant must already be enrolled at a German university at the time of application.
languageRequirements: Proof of sufficient German is mandatory even if the degree is taught in English: DSH level 2, TestDaF level 4, Goethe Zertifikat C1, DSD level II, or Telc C1 Hochschule. Applications must be submitted in German.
bondObligation: None (no formal return-home bond), but the foundation expects identification with and active commitment to the fundamental values of social democracy and ongoing volunteering / socio-political engagement
renewalConditions: Continued good academic performance and ongoing socio-political engagement; any income exceeding 400 EUR/month is credited against (deducted from) the scholarship
monthlyStipend: 934 EUR/month students; 1,200 EUR/month postgraduates (FES English page) — DAAD lists 992 EUR/month base for international students
benefits: Monthly maintenance stipend — FES English page: 934 EUR/month for students, 1,200 EUR/month for postgraduates (DAAD database lists a 992 EUR/month base amount for international students)
Family allowance of 276 EUR/month if applicable (DAAD lists a 160 EUR/month child allowance)
Non-material support (FES network, seminars, mentoring) so scholars have more time for their volunteering
Scholarship does not have to be repaid
requiredDocuments: Online application form (general personal details, professional and family background, your motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, details of your socio-political engagement) — submitted in German
Detailed CV with information on prior education and socio-political engagement (ausführlicher Lebenslauf)

Certificates / school-leaving (higher-education entrance) qualification, certificate of enrolment (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) and other proofs (Zeugnisse, Hochschulzugangsberechtigung, sonstige Nachweise)
Two expert references / Gutachten from university lecturers (for students and doctoral candidates)
Bachelor's / early-stage students: first graded performance records / first graded certificates of academic achievement
Proof of sufficient German language skills (DSH level 2, TestDaF level 4, Goethe Zertifikat C1, DSD level II, or Telc C1 Hochschule)

timeline.opens: Rolling — applications may be submitted at any time
timeline.deadline: No fixed annual deadline. Application cut-offs are tied to your stage of study: postgraduate/Master's programmes must apply by the end of the 1st semester; Bachelor's at least 3 semesters before the end of the standard period of study; diploma/magister/state-examination by the end of the 6th semester.
timeline.resultsBy: 3 to 7 months from application to decision (the selection committee meets 8-10 times a year; decision communicated within about a week of the committee sitting)
timeline.notes: Anchored at 2026-06: FES runs a rolling (no single annual deadline) intake, so there is no discrete open/close cycle; cycle is recorded as 2025-2026 to reflect the most recent known intake. The binding constraint is the per-stage application window above, not a calendar date. CRITICAL for Master's: FES does NOT fund 'short' courses of fewer than 3 semesters (e.g. typical 2-semester Master's), so apply only to a 3+ semester Master's and within the 1st semester.

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: FES does not publish a selection/acceptance rate. The DAAD database states the foundation awards 'up to 40 scholarships per year' for international students, but gives no applicant-pool figure, so no rate can be derived.

mustKnow: NOT an entry route from abroad: you must ALREADY be enrolled and studying at a German state/state-recognised university at the time you apply (FES: 'You are already studying in Germany at the time of your application'). There is no pathway to come to Germany on this scholarship.

German language is mandatory EVEN for English-taught programmes: you must prove DSH level 2 / TestDaF level 4 / Goethe Zertifikat C1 / DSD level II / Telc C1 Hochschule, and the entire application is submitted in German.

Short Master's degrees are excluded: FES does not fund a course of study shorter than 3 semesters (explicitly 'for example 2-semester Master's degree programmes'), and Master's applicants must apply by the end of their 1st semester.

Two-stage, multi-interview selection: online form first, then (if invited) full documents + two academic references, then a subject interview with a Vertrauensdozent/in and a second interview with a member of the selection committee before the committee decides; whole process takes 3-7 months.
Values requirement: applicants must demonstrate socio-political engagement and identify with the fundamental values of social democracy — this is a genuine selection criterion, not a formality.
OECD nationals are not eligible; this award is specifically for the Global South / post-Soviet / eastern-European students. Bangladesh qualifies.

Living stipend only — German public universities charge no tuition, so this funds your maintenance (and health insurance/family allowance), not a tuition fee; income over 400 EUR/month reduces the grant.
